summary: Wakefulness-promoting stimulant-like medication used for excessive daytime sleepiness. In psychiatry, it’s most often used off-label as an add-on for depression-related fatigue, low energy, and hypersomnia—but it can also worsen anxiety and insomnia.
description: Modafinil helps you stay awake and feel more mentally “switched on.” It’s FDA-approved for narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnea–related sleepiness (when the sleep apnea is already being treated), and shift work sleep disorder. In psych settings, it’s sometimes used off-label as an antidepressant add-on when depression comes with heavy fatigue, low drive, and sleeping too much. The tradeoff: it can trigger anxiety, insomnia, irritability, and in rare cases mania or psychosis. Serious rashes and allergic reactions are rare but can be life-threatening—any new rash needs urgent attention. Modafinil also weakens hormonal birth control, so contraception planning matters.
patient_summary: Modafinil is a wakefulness medication that can help with daytime sleepiness and “no energy” depression symptoms (especially hypersomnia + anergia). It’s not a chill pill—it’s more like flipping the lights on in your brain. That can be amazing for fatigue, but rough if you’re already anxious or struggling with insomnia. Watch for headache, nausea, jitteriness, and sleep disruption. Rare but serious risks include severe rash (SJS/TEN), allergic reactions, and new or worsened mania/psychosis. It also reduces the effectiveness of hormonal contraception during treatment and for at least a month after stopping.

primary.context: FDA-approved to improve wakefulness in adults with excessive sleepiness associated with narcolepsy.
FDA-approved to improve wakefulness during work shifts in people with shift work sleep disorder when nonpharmacologic strategies aren’t enough.

secondary.context: FDA-approved for persistent excessive daytime sleepiness in obstructive sleep apnea when the underlying obstruction is being adequately treated (eg, CPAP) and other causes of sleepiness have been ruled out.

off_label.context: Sometimes used as antidepressant augmentation in refractory depression when the symptom cluster is fatigue, low drive (anergia), and hypersomnia.
Used off-label for idiopathic hypersomnia; dosing is similar to narcolepsy, but evidence is more limited.
Sometimes used off-label for MS-related fatigue; doses above 200 mg/day have not consistently shown better results.
May be tried off-label for Parkinson disease–related excessive daytime sleepiness in select patients; data are limited and mixed.

therapeutic_response.display: Often noticeable same day; physiologic increases in heart rate and blood pressure have been reported within ~2 hours of dosing

common_adverse_effects.incidence: Very common (reported up to ~34% in adults)
common_adverse_effects.notes: This is the number one reason people quit. Hydration, food, and dose timing can help. If headaches are severe or persistent, the dose may be too high—or this may not be the right med for you.
Taking it with food can reduce nausea even though food may delay absorption. If you’re queasy all day, you shouldn’t have to suffer through it—adjustments are reasonable.

common_adverse_effects.incidence: ~5% in labeling (can be higher in real life if dosing is late)
common_adverse_effects.notes: This is a timing problem until it’s not. Morning dosing is safest. If sleep is fragile, this medication can destabilize it.
If you’re prone to panic or baseline anxiety, modafinil can feel like a stress amplifier. Dose reduction or stopping is sometimes the correct move.

common_adverse_effects.effect: Palpitations / Increased heart rate or blood pressure
common_adverse_effects.notes: If you’re getting chest pain, significant palpitations, or sustained high blood pressure, don’t push through—get evaluated.

serious_risks.risk: Severe skin reactions (SJS/TEN) and serious rash: blistering, peeling skin, mouth sores, fever, facial swelling. MEDICAL EMERGENCY.
Multi-organ hypersensitivity (DRESS-like reactions): rash plus fever and organ involvement (eg, hepatitis, myocarditis). MEDICAL EMERGENCY.
Psychiatric activation: mania, psychosis, severe agitation, hallucinations, delusions, aggressive behavior. Stop and seek urgent care.
Suicidal ideation: reported; treat as urgent, especially if mood destabilizes or agitation spikes.
Serious cardiovascular events (postmarketing): arrhythmias (including torsades de pointes), cardiomyopathy, heart failure—rare but high stakes.

contraindications.contraindication: Known hypersensitivity to modafinil, armodafinil, or any component of the formulation

precautions: Severe skin reactions (SJS/TEN) and multi-organ hypersensitivity: stop medication and seek urgent care with any rash, fever, mouth sores, facial swelling, or systemic symptoms
Psychiatric effects: can trigger or worsen agitation, anxiety, irritability, mania, psychosis, and suicidal thoughts—especially in people with prior psychiatric history
Cardiovascular effects: chest pain, hypertension, palpitations, tachycardia have been reported; serious arrhythmias and cardiomyopathy have been reported postmarketing
Pregnancy risk signal: registry data suggest increased risk of major congenital malformations; avoid use in pregnancy unless there is no safer alternative
Birth control interaction: reduces effectiveness of steroidal/hormonal contraception during treatment and for ≥1 month after stopping
Shift worker risk pattern: sleep disruption plus stimulant-like activation can unmask mood instability in vulnerable patients
Controlled substance (C-IV): lower abuse potential than amphetamines, but misuse and overuse can still happen

interactions.interactant: Hormonal contraception (pill, patch, ring, implant, some IUD hormone systems, depot injections)
interactions.mechanism: Reduced contraceptive effectiveness due to CYP3A4 induction (pregnancy risk).
interactions.action: Use effective non-hormonal contraception or add a reliable barrier method during modafinil therapy and for ≥1 month after stopping.

interactions.interactant: CYP3A4 substrates (examples: some antipsychotics, benzodiazepines, certain calcium-channel blockers, some statins, cyclosporine)
interactions.mechanism: Modafinil is a moderate CYP3A4 inducer and a minor CYP3A4 substrate; it can lower levels of some medications, reducing effectiveness.
interactions.action: If you notice a medication “stopping working” after starting modafinil, this is a prime suspect. Clinicians may need dose adjustments or alternatives.

interactions.interactant: CYP2C19 substrates (examples: diazepam, phenytoin, some TCAs and SSRIs depending on metabolism)
interactions.mechanism: Modafinil weakly inhibits CYP2C19, which can raise levels of some medications and increase side effects.
interactions.action: Watch for increased sedation, cognitive slowing, or toxicity signals depending on the paired medication. Adjustments may be needed.

interactions.mechanism: Higher risk of excessive sympathetic effects (blood pressure/heart rate issues) and activation.
interactions.action: Avoid combination unless a specialist is intentionally managing it.

interactions.interactant: Other stimulants (amphetamine, methylphenidate) or high-caffeine intake
interactions.mechanism: Stacked stimulation: anxiety, insomnia, tachycardia, blood pressure increases, agitation.
interactions.action: Start low, track sleep and vitals, and don’t pretend your body won’t notice the combo.

interactions.mechanism: Unpredictable effects on judgment and intoxication; may increase risk-taking or worsen sleep disruption.
interactions.action: If you drink, keep it minimal and watch how you respond. If you have a history of substance misuse, this is a higher-risk zone.

monitoring_requirements.parameter: Blood pressure and heart rate at baseline and periodically (more frequent if there is cardiac history or dose escalation)
Sleep quality and timing: insomnia, reduced total sleep time, fragmented sleep, circadian disruption (especially in shift workers)
Psychiatric symptoms: new or worsening anxiety, agitation, irritability, depression, suicidal thoughts, hallucinations, paranoia, mania-like activation
Skin and hypersensitivity: monitor for rash, fever, mucosal sores, facial swelling, systemic symptoms; stop medication immediately if suspected
Pregnancy status within about 1 week prior to initiation in females of reproductive potential; confirm contraception plan and counsel on reduced hormonal contraceptive effectiveness
Functional outcomes: daytime alertness, ability to complete tasks, safety (driving/workplace), and whether the medication is improving life versus just adding stimulation

special_populations.pregnancy: Avoid use in pregnancy when possible. Registry data have suggested an increased risk of major congenital malformations with in utero exposure. If there is no safer alternative and modafinil is being considered, document risk-benefit clearly and involve obstetric care. Pregnancy status should be evaluated shortly before starting in people of reproductive potential.
special_populations.lactation: Armodafinil (active metabolite) is present in breast milk. The manufacturer recommends caution. If used while breastfeeding, monitor the infant for irritability, poor feeding, or sleep disruption and discuss alternatives when feasible.
special_populations.pediatric: Not FDA-approved for pediatric use for any indication. Serious skin reactions and psychiatric events have been observed in children and adolescents; use is generally avoided unless benefits clearly outweigh risks and other options have failed.
special_populations.geriatric: Older adults may clear the medication more slowly and may be more sensitive to sleep disruption, blood pressure changes, and agitation. Start lower and reassess frequently.
special_populations.renal_impairment: No adjustment generally needed; use caution in severe renal disease due to accumulation of an inactive metabolite.
special_populations.hepatic_impairment: Severe hepatic impairment: reduce dose by 50%. Mild-to-moderate impairment: no specific adjustment provided in labeling, but use caution and titrate conservatively.

pharmacokinetics.absorption: Well absorbed; food may delay absorption but does not reduce overall bioavailability
pharmacokinetics.peak_plasma: 2 to 4 hours (may be delayed ~1 hour with food)
pharmacokinetics.food_effect: Food delays absorption but does not affect bioavailability

dosing.titration: Modafinil is usually taken in the morning. If twice-daily dosing is used, the second dose is typically around midday to avoid insomnia. Shift work dosing is different: a single dose about an hour before the work shift starts.

discontinuation.taper_guidance: Modafinil isn’t known for dangerous, seizure-type withdrawal like benzodiazepines. But stopping suddenly can still feel rough—especially if you were using it daily for daytime functioning.

sections.heading: What It's Used For
sections.text: Modafinil is a wakefulness-promoting medication. Officially, it’s for excessive daytime sleepiness. In psychiatry, it’s mostly used off-label when the problem isn’t “sadness” as much as being flattened by fatigue, low drive, and sleeping too much.
items: {link:condition:narcolepsy:Narcolepsy}: Improves wakefulness in adults with excessive sleepiness
{link:condition:obstructive-sleep-apnea:Obstructive sleep apnea–related excessive daytime sleepiness}: Only as an add-on when OSA is already being treated (eg, CPAP) and sleepiness is still a problem
{link:condition:shift-work-sleep-disorder:Shift work sleep disorder}: Helps with sleepiness during work shifts (taken before the shift)
off_label: {link:condition:major-depressive-disorder:Major depressive disorder} (refractory): Antidepressant augmentation for fatigue/anergia and hypersomnia
{link:condition:idiopathic-hypersomnia:Idiopathic hypersomnia}: Similar dosing to narcolepsy, but evidence is more limited
Parkinson disease–related excessive daytime sleepiness (data are mixed)
Refractory ADHD in children/adolescents (not FDA-approved; significant safety concerns)

sections.heading: What People Feel

I could stay awake without fighting my eyelids all day.
My mood wasn’t magically fixed, but I could actually do things again.
It helped the ‘I can’t move’ part of depression.

items.note: When it works in depression augmentation, it’s usually because fatigue and hypersomnia were the loudest symptoms.

quotes: I felt wired and weirdly on-edge.
My anxiety got louder, not quieter.
Great focus, but my body felt restless.
items.note: If anxiety, panic, or insomnia are already a problem, modafinil can make those worse.

quotes: If I took it too late, I paid for it that night.
I was awake… and then I was awake ALL night.
My sleep got lighter and more broken.
items.note: Timing matters. Morning dosing is the default; midday dosing is the latest most people can tolerate.

quotes: I got irritable and snappy fast.
It pushed me into a hyped-up place I didn’t like.
I started sleeping less and felt strangely invincible.
items.note: New or worsening mania/psychosis can happen, especially in people with bipolar spectrum risk or prior psychotic symptoms.

sections.intro: This medication has a very “switch-on” vibe for some people—and a very “too much coffee” vibe for others:

sections.heading: How Fast It Works
sections.text: Modafinil is usually a same-day medication—if it’s going to help, you often feel it the first day or within a few days. It also hangs around long enough that late dosing can wreck your sleep.
key_points: 1-2 hours: Many people start to notice increased alertness (some physiologic effects like BP/HR increases have been reported within ~2 hours)
All day: Wakefulness effect often lasts through the workday
~15 hours: Effective half-life (meaning it can still be “in the system” well into the evening)

sections.heading: How Well It Works
sections.text: Modafinil is not a universal fix for depression or sleep issues. It’s best thought of as a targeted tool for excessive sleepiness and low-energy symptom clusters. When the core problem is fatigue, hypersomnia, or staying awake at the wrong time (shift work), it can be a meaningful quality-of-life medication. When the core problem is anxiety, agitation, or insomnia, it can make things worse.
sections.clinical_details: Clinically, response tends to be clearer in sleepiness syndromes (narcolepsy/OSA-related sleepiness/shift work disorder) and more mixed in depression augmentation. In depression, the best-case outcome is improved energy, daytime function, and reduced hypersomnia without triggering anxiety or insomnia. If activation symptoms show up early (restlessness, irritability, racing thoughts, decreased need for sleep), the risk-benefit math changes fast.

patient_counseling: Take it in the morning. If a second dose is used, take it around midday—not late afternoon.
If you develop a rash, stop the medication and get medical advice urgently. Don’t “wait it out.”
Tell your clinician right away if you notice agitation, panic-like symptoms, hallucinations, paranoia, or a sudden decrease in need for sleep.
Monitor blood pressure and heart rate, especially if you have cardiac history.

If you can become pregnant: check pregnancy status before starting, use effective contraception, and avoid relying on hormonal birth control alone while on modafinil and for at least 1 month after stopping.
This medication does not treat the cause of sleep apnea. If you have OSA, CPAP (or other OSA treatment) still has to be the foundation.

sections.intro: Modafinil interacts with liver enzymes in a way that can change levels of other meds. The biggest real-world issue: it can reduce the effectiveness of hormonal contraception.

sections.heading: Safe Discontinuation
sections.text: Modafinil isn’t known for dangerous, seizure-type withdrawal like benzodiazepines. But stopping suddenly can still feel rough—especially if you were using it daily for daytime functioning.
key_points: Common stop-effects: rebound sleepiness, fatigue, low motivation, and mood slump for a few days
If you’ve been on higher doses or long-term daily use, a short taper can be more comfortable (example: decrease by 50-100 mg every 3-7 days)
If insomnia, anxiety, or activation was the problem, stopping may actually improve sleep and calm within days
If you’re taking it as an antidepressant add-on, plan a stop strategy with your prescriber so you can distinguish “rebound fatigue” from depression relapse

sections.heading: Dosing Information
sections.text: Modafinil is usually taken in the morning. If twice-daily dosing is used, the second dose is typically around midday to avoid insomnia. Shift work dosing is different: a single dose about an hour before the work shift starts.

adult.daytime_sleepiness_initial: 100 to 200 mg PO once daily in the morning
adult.daytime_sleepiness_titration: Increase at ≥1-week intervals based on response and tolerability; commonly in 100 mg/day increments (some protocols use 200 mg/day increments)
adult.daytime_sleepiness_max: 400 mg/day (either 400 mg QAM or 200 mg BID: morning + midday); doses >200 mg/day often have limited added benefit
adult.shift_work: 200 mg PO as a single dose ~1 hour before the start of the work shift
adult.depression_augmentation_initial: 100 mg/day PO for 3 to 7 days, then increase to 200 mg/day (targeting fatigue/anergia and hypersomnia)
adult.depression_augmentation_titration: Based on response and tolerability, may adjust up to 400 mg/day; consider weekly adjustments
adult.older_adult: Consider starting lower (eg, 100 mg QAM) and titrate cautiously; oral clearance is reduced in older adults
adult.hepatic: Severe hepatic impairment: reduce to one-half of the usual recommended dose (clearance decreased and concentrations increased in cirrhosis)
adult.renal: No dosage adjustment necessary for any degree of kidney impairment; in severe chronic renal failure, an inactive metabolite can accumulate

sections.simple_explanation: Think of modafinil like a long-lasting wakefulness push. Morning dosing gives daytime benefit and reduces the chance you’ll be staring at the ceiling at 2 a.m. Midday split dosing can smooth coverage, but late dosing is a common insomnia trap.

Pregnancy status should be evaluated shortly before starting in people of reproductive potential.

sections.heading: Available Formulations
sections.text: Modafinil is available as an oral tablet. Most people take it once daily in the morning; some regimens split doses to morning + midday.
items: Tablets (US): Provigil 100 mg; Provigil 200 mg (scored); generic modafinil 100 mg and 200 mg
Tablets (Canada): Alertec 100 mg; multiple generics including 100 mg

sections.heading: Mechanism of Action
sections.text: The exact mechanism isn’t fully pinned down, but the headline is this: modafinil increases brain dopamine by blocking dopamine transporters (DAT). It also shifts other wakefulness circuits—changing activity in neurotransmitter systems tied to alertness (including effects involving norepinephrine, serotonin, and GABA). The end result is increased wakefulness and mental alertness, with a lower “classic amphetamine” feel for many people—but it can still be activating.

sections.heading: Place in Treatment Algorithm
sections.text: In psychiatry, modafinil is a niche tool—not a first-line antidepressant and not a medication you throw at anxiety. The sweet spot is residual fatigue, hypersomnia, and low drive that persist despite an otherwise solid depression plan (therapy + antidepressant optimization). Before using it, you want to rule out sleep apnea, medication side effects (sedating antidepressants/antipsychotics), insufficient sleep, and bipolar spectrum risk. If the patient has panic, insomnia, agitation, uncontrolled hypertension, or a history of mania/psychosis, the threshold to avoid it should be lower.

faqs.a: Modafinil is used to improve wakefulness in people with excessive daytime sleepiness. It’s FDA-approved for narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnea–related sleepiness (as an add-on when OSA is being treated), and shift work sleep disorder. In psychiatry, it’s sometimes used off-label as an add-on for depression when the main issues are fatigue, low energy (anergia), and sleeping too much.

It’s often described as “stimulant-like.” It promotes wakefulness and can feel activating, but it’s not identical to amphetamines. Mechanistically, it increases dopamine in the brain by blocking dopamine transporters, and it affects other alertness circuits too.

faqs.q: How long does modafinil take to work?
faqs.a: Many people notice effects the first day. Blood levels peak around 2 to 4 hours after a dose (food can delay that a bit). Because the effective half-life is about 15 hours, it can affect you into the evening—so timing is everything.

It can help specific depression symptoms—mainly fatigue, low drive, and hypersomnia—when used as augmentation in select cases. It’s not a universal antidepressant booster, and it can backfire if anxiety, agitation, or insomnia are already prominent.

faqs.q: Can modafinil worsen anxiety or insomnia?
faqs.a: Yes. Anxiety, nervousness, and insomnia are known side effects, and some people feel jittery or over-revved. If you’re prone to panic, have fragile sleep, or already feel activated, modafinil can make that worse—especially at higher doses or with late dosing.

faqs.q: What’s the biggest safety warning with modafinil?
faqs.a: Rash. Rare severe rashes like Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN), as well as serious hypersensitivity reactions, have been reported. Any new rash—especially with fever, mouth sores, facial swelling, or systemic symptoms—should be treated as urgent.

faqs.q: Can modafinil trigger mania or psychosis?
faqs.a: It can. New or worsened mania, psychosis, agitation, hallucinations, and delusions have been reported. This risk is higher in people with bipolar-spectrum vulnerability or a history of psychotic symptoms. If activation symptoms show up (less need for sleep, racing thoughts, impulsivity, paranoia), it’s a stop-and-reassess situation.

Yes. Modafinil can reduce the effectiveness of hormonal contraception by inducing liver enzymes (CYP3A4). People who can become pregnant should use effective contraception that doesn’t rely only on hormones during treatment and for at least 1 month after stopping.

It’s generally avoided. Registry data have suggested an increased risk of major congenital malformations with pregnancy exposure. If modafinil is being considered in someone who is pregnant or could become pregnant, the risk-benefit discussion needs to be explicit and documented, and safer alternatives should be prioritized when possible.

faqs.q: Do I need to taper off modafinil?
faqs.a: Usually not for medical safety the way you would with benzodiazepines. But stopping abruptly can cause rebound sleepiness and fatigue. If you’ve been on higher doses or long-term daily use, a short taper (like reducing 50–100 mg every few days) can be more comfortable.

faqs.q: What’s the typical dose for modafinil?
faqs.a: A common starting range is 100 to 200 mg once daily in the morning. Some patients go up to 400 mg/day, either as a single morning dose or split into morning + midday. For shift work sleep disorder, it’s typically 200 mg about 1 hour before the shift starts.
